Stage task — Pocketful stage 1: payments and settlements API

Build a complete HTTP service and place ALL files inside stage-1/ in the result repository at:
C:\Users\USER\band-work\pocketful-result

RECOMMENDED STACK: Python + FastAPI + SQLite (WAL mode) + passlib[bcrypt]
Dependencies to install at Docker build time: fastapi, uvicorn[standard], passlib[bcrypt], python-multipart

Deliverables (all inside stage-1/):
- Complete service source code
- Dockerfile (no internet at runtime; all deps installed at build time)
- RUN.md with single command to build and start the service

After all files are written, implementer must run:
git -C C:\Users\USER\band-work\pocketful-result add .
git -C C:\Users\USER\band-work\pocketful-result commit -m "stage-1: initial implementation"

Then run harness checks (activate venv first):
cd C:\Users\USER\dark-factory-wearedevs
.venv\Scripts\activate
python -m harness run --track pocketful --repo C:\Users\USER\band-work\pocketful-result --stage 1 --out C:\Users\USER\band-work\checks\pf-s1-run1

=== FULL SPECIFICATION ===

SERVICE BASICS:
- Listen on 0.0.0.0, port from PORT env var, default 8080
- All requests/responses: application/json; charset=utf-8
- Timestamps: RFC 3339 with explicit offset e.g. 2026-09-24T19:00:00+00:00
- Unknown fields in request body: ignore, never error
- Unknown query params: ignore
- IDs: opaque strings up to 64 characters
- Resource limits: 2 vCPU, 2 GiB RAM, 60s startup, 5s per request (10s for reset/export/import), up to 50 concurrent requests

MONEY RULES (critical - never violate these):
- All amounts are exact integers (minor units). No floats, no rounding errors.
- Sum of all wallet balances always equals total seeded by last POST /_test/reset
- No wallet balance may ever go negative, including transiently
- A payment request may move money at most once
- Arithmetic range: amount max 1000000000 on any request; balances fit in ±2^53

FIXTURE FORMAT (POST /_test/reset body):
{
"currency": "EUR",
"minor_units": 2,
"users": [
{ "id": "u_ada", "email": "ada@example.com", "password": "correct horse",
"display_name": "Ada", "handle": "ada", "balance": 10000 },
{ "id": "u_bob", "email": "bob@example.com", "password": "correct horse",
"display_name": "Bob", "handle": "bob", "balance": 2500 }
],
"payments": [
{ "id": "p_1", "from_user_id": "u_ada", "to_user_id": "u_bob",
"amount": 500, "note": "coffee", "visibility": "public" }
],
"requests": [
{ "id": "rq_1", "requester_id": "u_bob", "payer_id": "u_ada",
"amount": 1200, "note": "taxi", "status": "pending" }
],
"settlement_operator_ids": []
}
- balance in fixture is final balance AFTER seeded payments applied. Do NOT replay payments against balances.
- Seeded users must log in with given password immediately (store bcrypt hash)
- balance below zero in fixture → 422 validation_failed, change nothing
- minor_units is 0, 2 or 3

ENDPOINTS:

GET /health → 200 {"status": "ok"} (no auth required)

POST /_test/reset (no auth, 10s timeout)
- Replace ALL state with fixture
- Return 204 on success
- Return 422 validation_failed if any balance < 0

GET /_test/export (no auth, 10s timeout)
- Return 200 {"track": "pocketful", "format_version": 1, "state": <opaque json>}
- Atomic read-only snapshot of all state

POST /_test/import (no auth, 10s timeout)
- Body is exact output of export
- Atomically replace all state, return 204
- Missing fields / wrong track or version → 422 validation_failed

POST /auth/signup (no auth required)
Body: {"email": "a@example.com", "password": "correct horse", "display_name": "Ada"}
→ 201 {"user_id": "u_1", "display_name": "Ada", "token": "..."}
Handle derived from email: take local part, lowercase, replace chars outside [a-z0-9_] with _, truncate to 20 chars
New users start with balance 0
Errors:
- Email already registered → 409 email_taken
- Password shorter than 8 chars → 422 validation_failed
- Email not of form local@domain → 422 validation_failed
- Derived handle already taken → 409 handle_taken (no account created)

POST /auth/login (no auth required)
Body: {"email": "a@example.com", "password": "correct horse"}
→ 200 {"user_id": "u_1", "display_name": "Ada", "token": "..."}
Errors:
- Wrong password or unknown email → 401 unauthenticated
Tokens never expire. Multiple valid tokens per account allowed.
Passwords MUST be stored with bcrypt/scrypt/argon2. No plaintext.

ALL REMAINING ENDPOINTS REQUIRE: Authorization: Bearer <token>
Missing/invalid token → 401 unauthenticated

GET /me → 200
{"user_id": "u_ada", "display_name": "Ada", "handle": "ada", "balance": 10000, "currency": "EUR", "minor_units": 2}

POST /payments (requires Idempotency-Key header)
Body: {"to_handle": "bob", "amount": 1500, "note": "dinner", "visibility": "public"}
note optional defaults "". visibility optional defaults "public".
→ 201 {
"payment_id": "p_7", "from_user_id": "u_ada", "from_handle": "ada",
"to_user_id": "u_bob", "to_handle": "bob", "amount": 1500, "currency": "EUR",
"note": "dinner", "visibility": "public", "request_id": null,
"created_at": "2026-09-24T11:04:03+00:00"
}
Debit and credit are ONE atomic step.
Errors:
- Balance below amount → 409 insufficient_funds
- amount < 1 or > 1000000000 or not integer → 422 validation_failed
- to_handle is caller's own handle → 422 self_payment
- note longer than 200 chars → 422 validation_failed
- visibility not public/private → 422 validation_failed
- No user with that handle → 404 not_found

POST /requests (requires Idempotency-Key header)
Body: {"payer_handle": "ada", "amount": 1200, "note": "taxi"}
Caller is the requester. Payer's balance NOT checked here.
→ 201 {
"request_id": "rq_4", "requester_id": "u_bob", "requester_handle": "bob",
"payer_id": "u_ada", "payer_handle": "ada", "amount": 1200, "currency": "EUR",
"note": "taxi", "status": "pending", "payment_id": null,
"created_at": "2026-09-24T11:06:10+00:00"
}
Errors:
- amount < 1 or > 1000000000 or not integer → 422 validation_failed
- payer_handle is caller's own handle → 422 self_request
- note longer than 200 chars → 422 validation_failed
- No user with that handle → 404 not_found

POST /requests/{id}/pay (requires Idempotency-Key, only the payer)
Body: {"visibility": "private"} (optional, default "public")
→ 201 with payment object (same shape as POST /payments), request_id set to this request
Request becomes "paid" and carries new payment_id
Errors:
- Request not pending → 409 request_not_pending
- Payer balance below amount → 409 insufficient_funds
- Caller is not the payer → 403 forbidden
- Unknown request → 404 not_found
Replay of successful payment → 200 with original body (no additional money moved)

POST /requests/{id}/decline (only payer, NO idempotency key)
→ 200 with request object, status: "declined"
Declining already-declined → 200 with current state (not an error)
paid or cancelled → 409 request_not_pending
Not the payer → 403 forbidden

POST /requests/{id}/cancel (only requester, NO idempotency key)
→ 200 with request object, status: "cancelled"
Cancelling already-cancelled → 200 (not an error)
paid or declined → 409 request_not_pending
Not the requester → 403 forbidden

GET /requests?direction=incoming&status=pending&limit=50&offset=0
Returns requests where caller is requester OR payer. Newest first.
direction: "incoming" (caller is payer), "outgoing" (caller is requester), absent = both
status: "pending"/"paid"/"declined"/"cancelled", absent = all
limit: default 50, range 1-200. offset: default 0, must be >= 0
Unknown direction or status value → 422 validation_failed
→ {"requests": [...], "has_more": false}

POST /splits (requires Idempotency-Key)
Body: {"amount": 3000, "participant_handles": ["ada", "bob", "cy"], "note": "dinner"}
Creates one pending request per participant EXCEPT the caller, with caller as requester.
ROUNDING RULE: shares are whole integers summing exactly to amount, differing by at most 1.
Larger shares go to FIRST participants in order.
Examples: 1000/3 → [334,333,333]. 10/3 → [4,3,3]. 1/3 → [1,0,0]
→ 201 {
"split_id": "sp_2", "amount": 3000, "currency": "EUR", "note": "dinner",
"shares": [{"handle":"ada","amount":1000},{"handle":"bob","amount":1000},{"handle":"cy","amount":1000}],
"requests": [<request for bob>, <request for cy>],
"created_at": "..."
}
shares includes caller, requests excludes caller. Both in participant_handles order.
Caller-only split is valid: creates zero requests, returns "requests": []
Errors:
- amount < 1 or > 1000000000 or not integer → 422 validation_failed
- participant_handles empty or contains duplicate → 422 validation_failed
- note longer than 200 chars → 422 validation_failed
- Any handle unknown → 404 not_found

GET /activity?limit=50&offset=0
Returns payments visible to caller: public payments OR caller is sender/receiver. Newest first.
Requests NEVER appear here.
→ {"payments": [...], "has_more": false}
limit/offset same rules as GET /requests

POST /settlements (requires operator token + Idempotency-Key)
Only users listed in settlement_operator_ids from fixture may call this.
Non-operator authenticated user → 403 forbidden
Body: {"transfers": [{"from_handle": "ada", "to_handle": "bob", "amount": 100}, ...]}
1 to 32 transfer objects. defaults: note="", visibility="public"
ALL transfers commit atomically or NONE do.
Affordable = every wallet's balance after ALL transfers >= 0
→ 201 {"settlement_id": "...", "committed_at": "...", "payments": [...]}
Each payment has settlement_id linking the batch; non-settlement payments have null settlement_id
Errors:
- Unknown handle → 404 not_found
- Self-transfer → 422 self_payment
- Malformed batch → 422 validation_failed
- Collective insufficient funds → 409 insufficient_funds
Entry errors checked in input order before funds check.

IDEMPOTENCY (applies to: POST /payments, POST /requests, POST /requests/{id}/pay, POST /splits, POST /settlements):
Header: Idempotency-Key: <string 1-255 chars>
Scoped to authenticated user. Different users can use same key string independently.
- Header absent or empty → 400 missing_idempotency_key
- First use → normal response (201)
- Replay (same key + same body) → 200, identical body
- Same key, different body → 409 idempotency_key_reuse
- Key reused after original 4xx → treated as first use
"Same body" = same JSON value after parsing (key order and whitespace irrelevant)
For concurrent identical requests: exactly one returns 201, others return 200
Idempotency key check happens BEFORE field validation when key is already claimed

ERROR FORMAT (all 4xx and 5xx):
{"error": {"code": "insufficient_funds", "message": "any human readable text"}}

ERROR CODES:
- 400 malformed_request: unparseable body or field of wrong JSON type
- 400 missing_idempotency_key: required header absent or empty
- 401 unauthenticated: missing/malformed/unknown bearer token
- 403 forbidden: authenticated but not permitted
- 404 not_found: no such resource or not visible to caller
- 409 idempotency_key_reuse: key used with different body
- 409 email_taken, handle_taken, request_not_pending, insufficient_funds
- 422 validation_failed: missing field, rule violated, invalid format
- 422 self_payment, self_request

QUERY PARAM VALIDATION:
- limit: integer 1-200. offset: integer >= 0.
- Integer query params must be plain decimal digits: "1e9", "4.0", "+4" → 422 validation_failed

Harness check command (run after implementer commits):
cd C:\Users\USER\dark-factory-wearedevs
.venv\Scripts\activate
python -m harness run --track pocketful --repo C:\Users\USER\band-work\pocketful-result --stage 1 --out C:\Users\USER\band-work\checks\pf-s1-run1

Do not ask the human for input. Resolve all decisions from this spec. If harness fails, implementer must fix and recommit, then reviewer re-checks. Repeat until harness passes stage 1 or a concrete blocker is found. Report final outcome to the human.
ACP v1 capabilities: supported [session/load, session/resume, session/close]; not advertised []; auth methods [Login with opencode (opencode-login)]

2. Delegate to implementer with the full task
3. When implementation is done, delegate to reviewer
4. Run harness checks
5. Report outcome

The message got interpreted by shell — likely due to unescaped characters like `;` splitting commands... Actually I used `;` inside the quoted string, that's fine. The error "unexpected argument 'Then'" suggests part of the message got split. Probably the `!` or some character. Actually likely issue: message contains `<` characters which PowerShell redirection... Inside double quotes `<` is fine, but the message also contains `"..."` unescaped sequences — I escaped with backslash `\"`, but PowerShell doesn't treat `\"` as escape; it uses `""` or backtick. So the quotes broke the string and splitting occurred.

Better: write message to a file and use `--file` or use jam with stdin? Let me check `jam send --help`. Alternatively use single quotes around the whole thing in PowerShell — single quotes preserve everything except single quotes. The message contains apostrophes like "caller's". Hmm.

Safest: write the message to a temp file and pass it. Check if send supports reading content from a file.
Use --body-file. Write the handoff text to a file, then send with --body-file.

SERVICE BASICS: Listen on 0.0.0.0, PORT env var default 8080; JSON responses application/json; charset=utf-8; RFC 3339 timestamps with explicit offset; unknown body fields and query params ignored; IDs opaque up to 64 chars; 5s per request (10s reset/export/import); up to 50 concurrent.

MONEY RULES: exact integer minor units, no floats; sum of balances == total seeded by last reset; no negative balances ever; each payment request moves money at most once; amount max 1000000000; balances within ±2^53.

Fixture: {currency, minor_units (0/2/3), users[{id,email,password,display_name,handle,balance}], payments[...], requests[...], settlement_operator_ids[...]}. Fixture balance is final balance AFTER seeded payments — do not replay. Seeded users can log in immediately (bcrypt hash). Negative fixture balance → 422 validation_failed, change nothing.

Endpoints:
- GET /health → 200 {"status":"ok"}, no auth.
- POST /_test/reset: replace ALL state, 204; 422 validation_failed if any balance < 0.
- GET /_test/export: 200 {"track":"pocketful","format_version":1,"state":...}; atomic snapshot.
- POST /_test/import: exact export body replaces state, 204; missing fields/wrong track or version → 422.
- POST /auth/signup {email,password,display_name} → 201 {user_id,display_name,token}; handle from email local part, lowercase, non [a-z0-9_]→_, truncate 20; balance 0. Errors: 409 email_taken; 422 if password<8, bad email; 409 handle_taken (no account).
- POST /auth/login {email,password} → 200 same shape; wrong → 401 unauthenticated. Tokens never expire, multiple tokens allowed, bcrypt/scrypt/argon2 only.
- All other endpoints: Authorization: Bearer <token>; missing/invalid → 401.
- GET /me → {user_id,display_name,handle,balance,currency,minor_units}.
- POST /payments (Idempotency-Key): {to_handle, amount, note?"", visibility?"public"} → 201 payment {payment_id,from_user_id,from_handle,to_user_id,to_handle,amount,currency,note,visibility,request_id:null,created_at,settlement_id presumably null}. Atomic debit+credit. Errors: 409 insufficient_funds; 422 invalid amount (<1, >1e9, non-int), self_payment (caller's own handle), note>200, visibility not public/private; 404 unknown handle.
- POST /requests (Idempotency-Key): {payer_handle, amount, note?} → 201 request {request_id,requester_id,requester_handle,payer_id,payer_handle,amount,currency,note,status:"pending",payment_id:null,created_at}. No payer balance check. Errors: 422 invalid amount, self_request, note>200; 404 unknown handle.
- POST /requests/{id}/pay (Idempotency-Key, payer only): {visibility?"public"} → 201 payment with request_id set; request→paid with payment_id. Errors: 409 request_not_pending; 409 insufficient_funds; 403 not payer; 404 unknown. Successful replay → 200 original body, no extra money.
- POST /requests/{id}/decline (payer, NO idempotency key): 200 request status declined; already-declined 200; paid/cancelled 409; not payer 403.
- POST /requests/{id}/cancel (requester, NO idempotency key): 200 request status cancelled; already-cancelled 200; paid/declined 409; not requester 403.
- GET /requests?direction=incoming|outgoing|absent&status=pending|paid|declined|cancelled|absent&limit&offset: caller is requester OR payer; newest first; incoming=payer, outgoing=requester; limit 1-200 default 50; offset >=0 default 0; unknown value → 422. → {"requests":[...],"has_more":false}.
- POST /splits (Idempotency-Key): {amount, participant_handles, note?} → 201 {split_id,amount,currency,note,shares:[{handle,amount}...],requests:[...],created_at}. One pending request per participant EXCEPT caller (caller=requester). Rounding: exact integer sum, differ ≤1, larger shares to FIRST participants. Examples: 1000/3→[334,333,333]; 10/3→[4,3,3]; 1/3→[1,0,0]. shares include caller, requests exclude caller, both in handle order. Caller-only split → requests []. Errors: 422 invalid amount / empty or duplicate handles / note>200; 404 unknown handle.
- GET /activity?limit&offset: payments visible to caller (public OR caller sender/receiver), newest first, never requests → {"payments":[...],"has_more":false}.
- POST /settlements (operator + Idempotency-Key): only settlement_operator_ids may call; else 403. {transfers:[{from_handle,to_handle,amount,note?"",visibility?"public"}]}, 1-32. IDEMPOTENCY (POST /payments, /requests, /requests/{id}/pay, /splits, /settlements): Idempotency-Key 1-255 chars, scoped to authenticated user. Absent/empty → 400 missing_idempotency_key. import ssl
```python
_orig = ssl.create_default_context
_cache = {}
def _cached(*args, **kwargs):

        hash(key)
    except TypeError:
        return _orig(*args, **kwargs)
    if key not in _cache:
        _cache[key] = _orig(*args, **kwargs)
    return _cache[key]
ssl.create_default_context = _cached
```

Caveat: sharing one SSLContext across many httpx clients. Is that safe? SSLContext is thread-safe for creating connections; httpx transports each create their own connections from the context. Reuse is standard practice (it's why `verify=False` or passing an ssl.SSLContext as `verify` is supported — httpx accepts an SSLContext instance and uses it directly). One risk: httpx might mutate the context (set verify_mode, load cert chains into it).
